subject: design
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (Coverage, Philosophy of the skill, Verification, Do NOT Use When) and established qualitative-synthesis practice (Kawakita's KJ affinity method, IDEO field guide, Stanford d.school, empathy maps, jobs-to-be-done).

cases.scenario: A researcher has 14 interview transcripts and proposes to 'read through them, get a feel for the patterns, and write up the top takeaways' by tomorrow.
cases.context: The team wants insight statements to take into an ideation workshop. No structured synthesis has happened yet.
cases.question: How should the agent guide the synthesis?
expected_flags: Download research first: extract atomic observations onto a shared surface, one per card, in the participant's words
Cluster bottom-up by proximity (affinity mapping); do not impose pre-existing categories
Name themes only after clusters form, not from an initial impression
Warns that impression-based 'top takeaways' reproduce the researcher's priors
expected_fix_hints: Move observations onto a wall/board as attributable cards before clustering
Produce 3-7 insight statements in observation + interpretation + implication form
absent_signals: Do not skip the downloading/clustering step
Do not name themes from a first-read impression

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: Download research first: extract atomic observations onto a shared surface, one per card, in the participant's words.

Surfaces this expected flag: Warns that impression-based 'top takeaways' reproduce the researcher's priors.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Move observations onto a wall/board as attributable cards before clustering.
Recommends this expected fix or action: Produce 3-7 insight statements in observation + interpretation + implication form.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not skip the downloading/clustering step.
Avoids this false-positive or out-of-scope signal: Do not name themes from a first-read impression.

cases.scenario: Early in synthesis, a teammate labels a cluster 'users want simplicity' and starts moving any card that mentions confusion, friction, or too many steps into it.
cases.context: The wall is filling up but the 'simplicity' cluster is becoming the biggest by far.
cases.question: How should the agent respond?
expected_flags: Flags premature abstraction — a theme named too early becomes a magnet pulling unrelated cards in
Recommends delaying naming; cluster by proximity first, name only when the cluster's shape is undeniable
Suggests breaking the over-broad cluster back into distinct, evidence-grounded sub-clusters
Notes 'simplicity' is too charitable/comfortable and may hide real distinct problems
expected_fix_hints: Re-cluster the 'simplicity' cards by what actually drove the confusion
Hold off on labels until cluster boundaries stabilize
absent_signals: Do not keep absorbing unrelated cards under one comfortable label

cases.scenario: A draft synthesis presents six bold themes, but several themes cannot be tied back to specific observations — they read like the team's pre-existing beliefs restated.
cases.context: Stakeholders are about to make roadmap decisions from these themes.
cases.question: What should the agent require before the themes are used?
expected_flags: Every theme must trace back to at least two specific cards, each attributable to a session/participant
Untraceable themes are impression-based and not defensible
Checks whether any insight contradicts a prior belief — if all are comfortable, synthesis was too charitable
Distinguishes observations / interpretations / implications rather than collapsing them
expected_fix_hints: Attach supporting cards to each theme or drop the theme
Surface at least one belief-contradicting insight
absent_signals: Do not ship themes with no evidentiary backing
Do not present prior assumptions as findings

cases.scenario: After two interviews, a designer wants to lock in three personas to 'design against' immediately.
cases.context: Patterns across the small sample are not yet stable.
cases.question: How should the agent respond to building personas now?
expected_flags: Persona drafting belongs only when patterns are stable enough to warrant archetypes
A persona built before patterns stabilize fossilizes a guess
Teams then optimize for a fictional user instead of real ones
Recommend more clustering/evidence before committing to personas
expected_fix_hints: Continue synthesis until clusters stabilize before drafting personas
Treat early personas as provisional hypotheses, not fixed targets
absent_signals: Do not lock personas from two interviews

cases.scenario: A team's synthesis output is a flat bullet list mixing 'users were confused', 'we should simplify onboarding', and 'people use it on Fridays' as if they were the same kind of statement.
cases.context: The output is meant to feed problem framing and ideation.
cases.question: How should the agent restructure the output?
expected_flags: Distinguish descriptive themes (what we heard) from interpretive insights (what it means) from point-of-view statements (what we will act on)
Each layer requires the previous one as evidence
Recast insights as observation + interpretation + implication
Output should be small and actionable (typically 3-7 themes)
expected_fix_hints: Rewrite each insight in observation + interpretation + implication form
Separate the three layers rather than mixing them in one list
absent_signals: Do not collapse observations, interpretations, and implications into one undifferentiated list

cases.scenario: A PM asks the research-synthesis owner to 'synthesize' a single competitor PDF report and, while they're at it, schedule five more user interviews.
cases.context: The PM conflates 'synthesis' with both document summarization and data collection.
cases.question: How should the agent scope the request?
expected_flags: Summarizing one PDF is out of scope — synthesis operates on a corpus for cross-session pattern extraction, not single-document summary
Running new interviews is out of scope — that is user-research (collecting primary data)
Offers the in-scope part: synthesize an existing corpus of qualitative evidence into themes
Correctly redirects rather than answering out of lane
expected_fix_hints: Hand document summarization to a summarization task; hand new interviews to user-research
Run user-research first, then research-synthesis on the resulting corpus
absent_signals: Do not treat single-document summarization as synthesis
Do not run new interviews under the synthesis banner

cases.scenario: A stakeholder asks the team to 'synthesize' the survey by computing response rates, average satisfaction scores, and a trend line over three quarters.
cases.context: The request uses the word 'synthesize' but is entirely about numbers.
cases.question: Is this research-synthesis work, and how should the agent respond?
expected_flags: Not research-synthesis — quantitative questions (counts, percentages, trends over time) need statistical analysis, not affinity methods
Research-synthesis operates on qualitative evidence (transcripts, notes, observations)
Redirects the numeric work to statistical/quantitative analysis
Offers in-scope help only if qualitative free-text responses exist to cluster
expected_fix_hints: Route the metrics to statistical analysis
Apply synthesis only to any open-ended qualitative responses
absent_signals: Do not apply affinity mapping to compute rates or trends
